answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public vault before it may bid, with one token granting one unit of influence. The contract releases the stake only after a fixed delay, so creating thousands of cedar-named accounts does not create influence for free: the attacker must buy and immobilize a proportional amount of capital, risking losses if identities misbehave. This raises the cost of a sybil swarm, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or prove that one account represents one person; a summit of independent checks can add that assurance.
